subject: Post-demo: Dedicated requirements, ops checklist, and GPU guidance
messages:

Subject: Post-demo: Dedicated requirements, ops checklist, and GPU guidance

Hi Samir — thanks again for the time today. Short recap + concrete asks so we can size Dedicated correctly.

TL;DR: ShopVerse is leaning Dedicated (predictable throughput + data isolation). To finalize a recommended pool size and GPU flavor we need a few concrete numbers from your side and will share a first-pass cost/latency tradeoff. I attached a capacity workbook with fields you can fill.

Recap of the call:
- Use case: sync product metadata + chat/assist queries (text generation) and a small reranking route for recommendations.
- Expected traffic pattern: high weekday spikes (marketing campaigns), low weekends.
- Primary constraint: sub-200ms p95 for the chat route under steady load.

Asks (please reply inline):
1) Routes & qps/TPS targets: what TPS do you expect at peak for each route (chat, generation, rerank)?
2) Token mix per request: average prompt tokens and average completion tokens per route (or examples).
3) Concurrency expectations: do you expect many concurrent short requests (burst traffic) or fewer long requests?
4) Latency SLO targets per route (p50/p95 if available).
5) Any hard requirements for on-prem/VPC (data residency) or is VPC Private Deployment optional?

Preliminary hardware guidance from our side (for planning):
- If chat is primary and you want <200ms p95 at medium-length completions (~256 tokens), H100 80GB pools are generally best for parallelism and KV cache scaling.
- A100 80GB is more cost-efficient for lower concurrency or when aggressive quantization is acceptable.
- Lower-cost T4/RTX options work for evaluation but will likely struggle with p95 <300ms at production scale.

Next steps: fill the workbook and send back by EOD Thursday; Vanessa will run a throughput projection and follow up with a recommended pool mix and estimated monthly run rate. I’ll loop procurement for contract/lead time.

Attachments: shopverse-capacity-workbook.xlsx, redwood-dedicated-sku-guide-v2.pdf

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Karthik — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers inline below, will push a filled workbook by tomorrow morning.

1) Routes / peak TPS (estimates):
- chat (customer-facing assistant): 220 TPS peak during campaigns (steady-state 80 TPS)
- generation (batch content gen for product descriptions): 30 TPS peak (mostly off-peak)
- rerank (recommendation score): 420 TPS spikes but very short completions (~12 tokens)

2) Token mix:
- chat: avg prompt 80 tokens, avg completion 140 tokens
- generation: avg prompt 40 tokens, avg completion 400 tokens
- rerank: avg prompt+completion ~12 tokens

3) Concurrency: we expect many concurrent short requests during campaigns (chat + rerank concurrency high).

4) Latency SLOs: chat p95 <= 200ms; rerank p95 <= 120ms; generation p95 <= 500ms (batch can be looser).

5) Data residency: VPC is preferred but not strictly required for MVP — procurement will confirm contract needs.

Questions back to you: given the rerank spikes (420 TPS) and chat peaks, do you recommend a single homogeneous pool or a split pool (low-latency H100 for chat + mixed A100 for generation/rerank)? Also curious about how KV cache sharing/sharding affects latency when you have mixed-token-length routes.

Thanks,
Samir

Samir — thanks for the detailed numbers, this is very helpful. High-level thoughts from ops/size perspective: please see recommendations below; I’ll run a throughput model once we get the workbook.

- Pool strategy: split pools are preferred here. Rationale: your rerank route is extremely high TPS but very short (12 tokens) — that favors dense GPU utilization with many concurrent streams, whereas chat requires lower tail latency for medium-length completions. Maintaining two pools (H100-based low-latency pool for chat; A100/quantized pool for rerank+generation) gives better cost/latency tradeoffs and enables targeted autoscaling.

- Suggested starting mix (POC):
  * Chat pool: 4 x H100-80GB nodes (aiming for ~250 TPS headroom, p95 <200ms).
  * Rerank pool: 6 x A100-80GB nodes using int8 quantization for rerank kernels (handles spikes up to ~600 TPS for short tokens).
  * Generation batch: start on the A100 pool during off-peak; if generation latency becomes critical, add 1–2 H100 nodes.

- Concurrency & batching knobs:
  * Use small dynamic batching window (5–10ms) for chat to keep p95 tight.
  * Aggressive batching for rerank (20–50ms) to maximize throughput.
  * Prefix KV cache: enable for chat to reduce compute per request if customers reuse context frequently.

- KV cache/sharding note: cache locality matters — if chat and rerank share the same model instance we can optimize KV reuse, but split pools mean separate caches. Given your rerank tokens are tiny, the cache benefit is marginal there; it’s most impactful for chat where context repeats.

Actionables:
- Karthik: please run a throughput projection with the workbook numbers (Neha will support).
- Neha: can you validate lead times for H100/A100 availability in us-west region and add a short ops-runbook note for autoscaling thresholds?

Attaching the SKU guide to help with preliminary cost math.

- Vanessa Ortiz

Ellie — thanks for the questions. Quick answers and next steps below; I’ll follow with a concise one-pager and cost estimate.

1) Committed discounts: yes — we offer tiered committed discounts for Dedicated (12m / 24m). Typical bands: 10% for 12m baseline, 18% for 24m (exacts depend on committed tokens and pool mix). We’ll include illustrative numbers in the one-pager.
2) SLA: standard Dedicated SLA is 99.9% with credit tiers; we can discuss enhanced SLAs for enterprise with additional support add-ons. I’ll include the SLA summary.
3) Billing: two-line model is common (base reserved capacity + usage overage by token/embedding). We can map to your finance preference.
4) Lead time: current estimate for H100 capacity in us-west is 6–8 weeks after PO (we’ll confirm based on availability at signing). A100 lead times are shorter (2–4 weeks typical).

Next steps: Neha will run the throughput projection in the workbook and I’ll deliver a recommended pool mix + 3-month cost projection by EOD Monday. Can we lock a 30-minute follow-up on Tuesday 9/21 at 10:00am PT to review? I’ll include Vanessa on ops notes and Ellie on the cost/contract summary.

Thanks —
